extracted.intended_audience: executive branch agencies, Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA), regulatory policy officials, and agency counsel/staff who design or review regulations
extracted.subtask_description: An Executive Order (EO 14094) that sets standards and procedures for modernizing regulatory review across executive-branch agencies, focusing on inclusive public participation, definitions of significant regulatory actions, OIRA meeting practices, and regulatory analysis requirements (including equity/distributive impacts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Significant regulatory action'
rubrics_metrics.description: “Significant regulatory action” means any regulatory action that is likely to result in a rule that may: (1) have an annual effect on the economy of $200 million or more (adjusted every 3 years by the Administrator of OIRA for changes in gross domestic product); or adversely affect in a material way the economy, a sector of the economy, productivity, competition, jobs, the environment, public health or safety, or State, local, territorial, or tribal governments or communities; (2) create a serious inconsistency or otherwise interfere with an action taken or planned by another agency; (3) materially alter the budgetary impact of entitlements, grants, user fees, or loan programs or the rights and obligations of recipients thereof; or (4) raise legal or policy issues for which centralized review would meaningfully further the President's priorities or the principles set forth in this Executive order, as specifically authorized in a timely manner by the Administrator of OIRA in each case.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EO amends Sec. 3(f) of EO 12866 to adopt this definition; the $200 million threshold is adjusted every 3 years by OIRA for GDP changes. This definition determines when centralized OIRA review applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative promotion of inclusive and meaningful public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent practicable and consistent with applicable law, regulatory actions should be informed by input from interested or affected communities; State, local, territorial, and Tribal officials and agencies; interested or affected parties in the private sector and other regulated entities; those with expertise in relevant disciplines; and the public as a whole. Opportunities for public participation shall be designed to promote equitable and meaningful participation by a range of interested or affected parties, including underserved communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general principle directing agencies to prioritize equitable, meaningful engagement when designing notice-and-comment and other participation opportunities. The EO repeatedly conditions implementation on practicability and applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify, respond to, and log petitions under 5 U.S.C. 553(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall, to the extent practicable and consistent with applicable law: (i) clarify opportunities for interested persons to petition for the issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule under 5 U.S.C. 553(e); (ii) endeavor to respond to such petitions efficiently, in light of agency judgments of available resources and priorities; and (iii) maintain, subject to available resources, a log of such petitions received, and share with the Administrator of OIRA, upon request, information on the status of recently resolved and pending petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates procedural expectations for transparent petition routes, timeliness of responses, and recordkeeping/sharing with OIRA to inform regulatory planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive engagement and use of accessibility and outreach best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: To inform the development of regulatory agendas and plans, agencies shall endeavor, as practicable and appropriate, to proactively engage interested or affected parties, including members of underserved communities; consumers; workers and labor organizations; program beneficiaries; businesses and regulated entities; those with expertise in relevant disciplines; and other parties that may be interested or affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These efforts shall incorporate, to the extent consistent with applicable law, best practices for information accessibility and engagement with interested or affected parties, including, as practicable and appropriate, community-based outreach; outreach to organizations that work with interested or affected parties; use of agency field offices; use of alternative platforms and media for engaging the public; and expansion of public capacity for engaging in the rulemaking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernize notice-and-comment to address mass, computer-generated, and falsely attributed comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator of OIRA, in consultation with relevant agencies, as appropriate, shall consider guidance or tools to modernize the notice-and-comment process, including through technological changes. These reforms may include guidance or tools to address mass comments, computer-generated comments (such as those generated through artificial intelligence), and falsely attributed comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs OIRA to develop guidance or technological tools to improve handling and analysis of high-volume or inauthentic public submissions; implementation is subject to practicability and applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA meeting access, efficiency, and transparency reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: To reduce the risk or appearance of disparate and undue influence in OIRA's review process, the Administrator of OIRA shall, to the extent practicable and consistent with applicable law: (i) provide information to facilitate the initiation of meeting requests regarding regulatory actions under OIRA review from potential participants not employed by the executive branch of the Federal Government who have not historically requested such meetings, including those from underserved communities; and (ii) implement reforms to improve procedures and policies with respect to OIRA's consideration of meeting requests initiated by persons not employed by the executive branch of the Federal Government regarding the substance of regulatory actions under OIRA review to further the efficiency and effectiveness of such meetings. These reforms may include: (A) efforts to ensure access for meeting requesters who have not historically requested such meetings; (B) discouraging meeting requests that are duplicative of earlier meetings with OIRA regarding the same regulatory action by the same meeting requesters; (C) consolidation of meetings by requester, subject matter, or any other consistently applied factors deemed appropriate to improve efficiency and effectiveness; and (D) disclosure of data in an open, machine-readable, and accessible format that includes the dates and names of individuals involved in all substantive meetings and the subject matter discussed during such meetings, as required by section 6(b)(4)(C)(iii) of Executive Order 12866, so as to better facilitate transparency and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets multiple procedural criteria: broaden access (esp. to those who haven't historically requested meetings), discourage duplicative requests, consolidate meetings when appropriate, and require machine-readable disclosure of meeting participants, dates, and subjects to improve transparency and reduce apparent undue influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory analysis must serve the public interest and recognize distributive impacts and equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory analysis should facilitate agency efforts to develop regulations that serve the public interest, advance statutory objectives, and are consistent with Executive Order 12866, Executive Order 13563, and the Presidential Memorandum of January 20, 2021 (Modernizing Regulatory Review). Regulatory analysis, as practicable and appropriate, shall recognize distributive impacts and equity, to the extent permitted by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a substantive analytic standard requiring agencies to incorporate equity and distributive-impact considerations into cost-benefit or regulatory analyses where practicable and lawful; it frames revisions to analytic guidance and tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise OMB Circular A-4 to implement equity/distributive-impact policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 1 year of the date of this order, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, through the Administrator of OIRA and in consultation with the Chair of the Council of Economic Advisers and representatives of relevant agencies, shall issue revisions to the Office of Management and Budget's Circular A-4 of September 17, 2003 (Regulatory Analysis), in order to implement the policy set forth in subsection (a) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates a timeline and interagency consultation (OIRA, CEA, relevant agencies) to update the primary federal guidance on regulatory analysis (Circular A-4) to reflect the EO's emphasis on distributive impacts and equity.
